Weapon-state = shot economy = damage (taxonomy 6). Test 13 requires an instantReload with fraction ~0.1026 OR an explicit note/unmodeled entry. RED under a silent drop, which would under-count shots fired over ~10 level-ups.
Self-heal: offensively inert alone but it is the on-recovery channel a teammate can consume (taxonomy 4). Test 13 requires a heal effect OR an explicit audit-text entry. RED under a silent drop.

Test 5 requires every burst-slot block to trigger on burstCast. RED under fullBurstEnter, which over-credits precisely in this fixture because helm is a second Burst III that can complete the chain without this unit casting.

Test 6 requires exactly ONE dot effect in the burst slot with durationSec 10 and intervalSec 1, and Hero-Level scaling either via perResource mult 20.87 or a static atkPct that is a whole-level multiple within the Lv-11 cap. RED under multiple/duplicated DoT instances (the engine never dedups), under a duration longer than the stated 10s on a repeating trigger, and under a level-free flat magnitude. Test 6b proves the damage is reachable (stripping it lowers the carry) and teammate-inert. The block target is deliberately NOT asserted: the sim has no enemy entity, so enemy-directed damage is authored caster-side.

fixtures: controlComp('guillotine-winter-slayer', true) only - liter (B1, Fire) / crown (B2, Iron) / carry (B3, Water) / helm (B3, Water), Fire boss. helm is kept ON deliberately: she is the only other Water Code ally, so she is the sole observable that separates 'all Water Code allies' from 'self' and from 'all allies', and as a second Burst III she is also what makes the burstCast-vs-fullBurstEnter trigger check non-vacuous. liter + crown are the out-of-scope controls. 4 hoisted 180s runs: base, plus three counterfactuals built with withPatchedOverride (strip non-self skill1 effects; strip every 1.81-magnitude buff in any slot; strip every damage-dealing effect from the burst slot) - all three patches are encoding-agnostic walks, not edits to a guessed block index. CAVEAT recorded on the fixture: Water has no elemental advantage against the Fire control boss, so every elemAdvantageDamagePct line is expected to be DAMAGE-INERT in this comp; all elemental assertions are therefore made on the buffApply event log (stat key, magnitude, target set), which is boss-element independent.
gaps: it.skip 'EXP ramp is monotonic over the fight' - proving the ramp directly needs the per-damage-event amount field, whose name is not pinned in the blind harness contract (it documents bucket / srcSlot / crit / core / inFullBurst / mult only). Covered indirectly by the growing-magnitude assertion (test 9) and the EXP-strip counterfactual (test 11b).

it.skip 'EXP accrual RATE matches (1-c)/6 + c/3 per normal hit' - MEASUREMENT-GATED: requiresCore is a fight-level core-exposure gate, not a per-hit core/non-core partition, so the engine cannot express the exact split between the two counters at a given core rate. The effective accrual rate, and therefore the whole Hero Level trajectory (and the burst DoT magnitude, which scales off it), is a flagged estimate until read off footage.

Hero Level cap of 11 vs the EXP cap of 100: 100 stacks / 10 = 10 level-ups, which reaches Lv 11 only if the unit starts at Lv 1. That reading is assumed throughout (it is also what makes the 'Hero Level 2 or above' clause meaningful at t=0) but is not independently verifiable from the prose - flagged, not asserted.
The 'Affects 1 enemy unit(s) with the highest final Max HP' target selector is unobservable: the sim has no enemy entity, so the DoT block's target field is not asserted.

The 10.26% partial reload and the 2.44% self-heal are asserted as modelled-or-documented only; their magnitudes have no observable consequence in this fixture (no HP pool, and a partial reload's shot-economy effect is not separable from the base cadence without a dedicated counterfactual).
